rgb: This indoor retail scene contains a dark slatted display wall at center-left, a white wall on its right with a light switch and floor outlet, a doorway at the far right, and a full-length mirror at the far left. Roughly 1 to 1.5 metres ahead, a white top hangs above a black-and-white striped garment on the slatted wall, with an orange promotional sign to the top’s right. In the first frame, the camera wearer looks toward the mirror and wall as a person wearing a plaid shirt, dark glasses, and a green lanyard appears partly along the bottom-left edge, holding a smartphone within 0.5 metres. During the second and third frames, the camera turns right and angles slightly downward toward the doorway (~1.5 to 2 metres away), while a white furry hat or garment being held at the left edge (~0.3 to 0.5 metres away) comes into view and partly blocks the striped garment on the slatted wall. In the fourth and fifth frames, the plaid-shirted person moves directly before the camera wearer at about 0.5 to 0.8 metres—within each other’s arm’s reach—and obscures the mirror and much of the slatted wall behind them. The person faces the camera wearer but lowers their head to view the smartphone held in both hands at chest height instead of making direct eye contact with the camera wearer.
depth: The monocular depth visualization represents the retail interior’s receding layout and follows a foreground person moving into the area directly before the camera wearer over five frames. In Frame 1, a bright foreground hand and phone at bottom-left (~0.3-0.5 m, within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach) appear before a mid-ground clothing display wall on the right (~1.2-1.8 m) and a dark mirror cavity on the left. In Frame 2, a bright item appears at the bottom-left corner (~0.5 m), ahead of the slatted clothing rack on the left (~1.2-1.5 m), while the white wall and dark doorway extend away on the right (~1.5-2.5 m). From Frames 3 through 5, a person comes in from the left at ~0.5-0.8 m and moves directly in front of the camera wearer at ~0.5-0.7 m (within both the camera wearer’s arm’s reach and that of the background rack ~1 m behind them). They face the camera wearer, with their downward-angled head appearing brightest in Frame 4 (~0.4-0.5 m). In Frame 5, their right hand holding a phone (viewer’s left, ~0.3-0.4 m) and raised left hand (viewer’s right, ~0.4-0.5 m) extend nearest to the camera in front of their chest, while the lower body stays outside the frame below. Relative to the RGB strip by itself, the depth map more clearly separates the approaching person, outstretched hands, and phone from the visually busy patterned garments and plaid shirt behind them, and also reveals the wall plane’s continuous left-to-right slant. Nevertheless, it handles the mirror in Frame 1 unreliably, depicting its reflection as a deep black void rather than a flat surface at ~1.2 m; compresses the hanging garments into the wall plane in Frames 2-3; and turns the background wall nearly black in Frames 4-5 because relative depth normalization changes when the person and hands approach very closely.
segmentation: After leaving Frame 1 wholly empty, the instance segmentation visualization supplies 2D outlines and class names for prominent areas in Frames 2-5. In Frame 2, it identifies the angled central wall (~1.5-2.0 m from the camera wearer), located between the unsegmented clothing rack on the left and doorway on the right. In Frames 3 and 4, it follows a pink mask labeled ‘person’ as it moves from the left (~0.5-0.8 m) into the center (~0.5-0.7 m, within arm’s reach), directly in front of the background wall mask and increasingly covering its left portion (~1 m behind the person). In Frame 5, the ‘person’ region fills the center-left foreground (~0.3-0.7 m) while the person faces the camera wearer, with their lower torso cut off by the bottom border. Two small intersecting regions labeled ‘tie’ appear over the chest where the green lanyard and handheld phone are located, within both the person’s and camera wearer’s arm’s reach (~0.3-0.6 m). Against the cluttered shop background, this visualization makes the 2D boundary where the approaching person’s outline occludes the background wall in Frames 3-4 immediately clear. It is nonetheless very unreliable: Frame 1 contains no detections; the flat white wall is incorrectly called a ‘refrigerator’ in Frames 2-4 and then disappears entirely in Frame 5; the lanyard-and-phone area is wrongly labeled ‘tie’ in Frame 5 while neither the phone nor hanging clothes are separately segmented; and the head, torso, and lifted arms are combined into one flat person mask, concealing relative 3D depth and orientation.
pose: The pose visualization draws yellow 2D body landmarks and magenta hand skeletons over black, staying entirely blank throughout Frames 1-4 and finding a skeleton only in Frame 5. There, the yellow trapezoid for the upper torso and the facial landmarks position the person in the center-left foreground (~0.5-0.7 m from the camera wearer, within arm’s reach). The person faces the camera wearer with their head tipped downward—the eye and nose landmarks lie below ear height, indicating a gaze toward the chest area—and everything below the hips falls outside the image at its bottom. Yellow arm connections depict both elbows spread outward on either side of the torso, with both wrists drawn together before the chest (~0.3-0.5 m from the camera wearer and separated from one another by ~0.15 m). At that location, the person’s right wrist (viewer’s left) supports the phone, while the left hand (viewer’s right) is lifted next to it. Compared with the RGB image alone, Frame 5’s skeleton directly identifies the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip locations despite the visually complex plaid flannel design and dark sunglasses. The pose output remains unreliable across the sequence, however: it misses the person completely in Frames 1, 3, and 4, including Frame 4 when the entire upper body and head are plainly visible; omits the magenta finger skeleton from the right hand holding the phone in Frame 5; and draws warped, elongated magenta lines on the motion-blurred left hand that incorrectly stretch toward the lower-right elbow.
